$comment: JRM Studio manifest. Source of truth for the cross-repo sync engine in sync/ (see docs/sync.md and sync/README.md), which reads this file on every run. Fields fall into three tiers. EXECUTED — repo, optIn.base, optIn.agents/skills/prompts/instructions, targetPaths and tokens decide which files are written where; getting one wrong changes the output. VERIFIED — mode selects the checkout evidence contract; framework and packageManager are checked when they apply but never decide a write. RECORDED — localAgents names locally authored roles/replacements used for handoff validation but never copied; optIn.health is native reliance, while optIn.workflows is the workflow availability declaration. Checkout inspection records actual backbone workflow uses with file, line, and immutable SHA; undeclared uses fail and available-but-unused entries are reported without failing because future adoption is intentional. Neither native kind is copied. DESCRIPTIVE — notes supplies human/agent context. Schema validation covers mode, mode-specific facts, repo, optIn, localAgents and tokens; integrity validation also enforces canonical agent, prompt, instruction, and workflow contracts. Real syncs, --check, and --work-dir inspect each existing member checkout before writes. Manifest-only --dry-run stays offline and cannot verify checkout facts. See sync/README.md#member-entries.

optInSyntax.$comment: Each member.optIn.<kind> is either the string "*" (all canon of that kind), an array of names, or false (opt out). base/runtime/copilot/attributes/health are booleans. base (AGENTS.md), runtime (agency.toml), copilot (.github/copilot-instructions.md) and attributes (.gitattributes) are four INDEPENDENT booleans: an infrastructure member that declines the studio operating guide must still be able to receive canonical MCP policy, Copilot-surface orientation, and LF normalization. attributes is a managed-region merge, so a member keeps its own binary/LFS/linguist rules outside the studio markers.

tokens.$comment: Vendored design tokens from the OTHER private backbone repo jrmoulckers/studio (package @jrm/tokens). Registry-free: the sync engine copies studio's committed dist/ tree verbatim into each opted-in member (Option A). The whole sourceBase tree is mirrored today; a future optional per-member `include` (array of sub-globs under sourceBase) may narrow this without a breaking schema change. Per-member opt-in lives in members[].tokens, kept separate from optIn because the source is an external repo, not the .github canon.

members.notes: New consumer web product. Adopts the full canonical layer.
Game-night scoring app. Adopts the canonical roster and keeps its committed design-engineer as an explicit local replacement, so only design-engineer is omitted from sync.

Product-specific platform and risk rules live in root/scoped overlays. The canonical AI layer is materialized atomically while finance-domain remains the only locally authored agent. Vendored tokens land at the repo root because @jrm/tokens now ships native Compose and Swift sources alongside the web artifacts, and all four platform apps (android, ios, web, windows) must reach one copy.
Pure-client media hub for books and audiobooks. Svelte/Vite PWA at repo root; first member to consume vendored @jrm/tokens.

Local-first game library PWA. Svelte 5 + Vite at repo root, IndexedDB via idb, vite-plugin-pwa. Separate bridge/ Cloudflare Worker (OAuth token exchange, KV cache, CORS allowlist) with its own toolchain, so this member is not backend-free. Opted in with "*": its partial canon set came from a hand-typed list in a scaffold script, not a curation decision, so freezing it would preserve a first-pass guess.

Native-first task system with a Svelte PWA, pnpm workspace, shared domain/contracts packages, Hono/SQLite server, and planned SwiftUI client. Upgraded from pre-bootstrap immediately when its application and root toolchain evidence landed.

Engineering authority under ADR-0003: architecture, frontend and backend engineering, data systems, security and privacy mechanisms, testing, performance, observability, and build/release engineering. A principles-and-implementations repository, so it takes the AI layer without base, health, workflows, or vendored tokens. It receives runtime and copilot independently of base so canonical MCP policy and Copilot-surface orientation still apply. The declared framework and packageManager are descriptive checkout facts, not an application claim: this is an npm workspace root publishing shared lint/format config packages, and Svelte is a devDependency because those packages lint Svelte consumers.

Product authority under ADR-0003: strategy, planning, business, discovery, experimentation, metrics, compliance obligations, delivery decisions, content operations, and product templates. Like Engineering it is a principles-and-implementations repository with no product toolchain, so base, health, workflows, and tokens stay off while the AI layer, MCP policy, and Copilot orientation are canonical. Token authoring instructions are excluded because Studio owns tokens.

Design and tooling kernel with local principles as the authoritative map for canonical roles. It retains the five general instruction contracts, including token authoring, without Homelab live-operations semantics. It declines the studio base guide in favor of its local one while still taking canonical MCP policy and Copilot orientation. Studio remains the token source, never its own vendored-token target.

Infrastructure-as-code and operations repository for Proxmox, self-hosted services, automation, backups, and runbooks. Its eight product-specific agents and local flat schema remain authoritative alongside the canonical roster; only agent compatibility and live infrastructure operations instructions are selected. Generic docs, skills, tokens, product workflow, and the studio base guide remain local or excluded, while canonical MCP policy and Copilot orientation apply. Its audited prompt subset is intentionally read-oriented: backlog, review, and hardened audit-first cleanup.

Windows device-management repository for shared and per-machine configuration. It selects infrastructure operations plus relevant generated-agent, skill, and docs rules, along with canonical MCP policy and Copilot orientation, while excluding token authoring, product fleet workflow, and the studio base guide.
